question: Q-078, Q-079 and Q-080 name simple-login.integration.3's reliance on `npm --prefix backend start` creating the service's tables in an empty database, the window before simple-login.integration.3 lands, and a `start` test on a database without the schema. Does simple-login.backend's header or Overview change for any of them?

options.label: header and Overview unchanged
options.consequence: Every clause the items name stays where it already lives: D3, D6, D8 and simple-login.backend.7 in the Phase Plan, and booking-api@v1's Development address (DEC-198, DEC-199). The Overview's closing sentence already sends readers to booking-api@v1 for what the node promises. This step changes no file.

options.label: add an Overview sentence on start behavior
options.consequence: The Overview would say that the service creates its tables in an empty database when it starts and that the rooms need no loading. That restates the Development address in a second home, which drifts when either changes, and corrects nothing the header or Overview now gets wrong.

why: Nothing in the header or Overview is false or missing for these items. Owns already names the pre-loaded rooms and the database; the Overview says bookings survive a restart and sends every promise visible outside the node to its contracts. The start behavior is D6 (one schema file, every statement IF NOT EXISTS, applied at every start) and D3 (the rooms are data in the service, no rooms table), and booking-api@v1's Development address now promises it. Q-078's question was answered at S21 (DEC-198). What remains in Q-079 and Q-080 is Phase Plan content, which a touch may not edit (hsdd-spec Touch). A header or Overview sentence these items made false, such as rooms loaded as rows or a separate schema command, would have required the edit.
evidence: hsdd/spec/simple-login.backend.md Owns, Overview, D3, D6, simple-login.backend.7 Scope

question: Q-080: every backend test runs on a database the D8 helper creates with the schema already applied, so nothing at the producer's gate proves the promise in booking-api@v1's Development address that simple-login.integration.3's global setup relies on (an empty database gets its tables at start). Does the backend's plan take a `start` test on a database without the schema, and by which step, since this touch may not edit the Phase Plan?

options.label: insert a phase-plan-append that rewrites simple-login.backend.7 in place
options.consequence: One more step in the run, plus a reconcile only if it emits entries. simple-login.backend.7's `start` test in server.test.ts starts the service on a database created without the schema and lists the four rooms with no bookings, then starts it again on the same database after a booking and still lists it; the D8 helper gains a way to create a database without the schema. The producer's gate proves both clauses of the Development address, and a later change that moves schema creation out of `start` fails the backend's gate instead of the integration's suite.

options.label: close as explained with no step
options.consequence: No step. simple-login.integration.3 proves the behavior on every run, since its global setup re-creates meeting_rooms_e2e empty, and D6's IF NOT EXISTS makes it hold by construction. A regression surfaces only in the integration's suite, which the hard edge on simple-login.backend.7 schedules after the backend ships, in a lane the backend developer does not run.

chosen: insert a phase-plan-append that rewrites simple-login.backend.7 in place
why: booking-api@v1's Development address now promises a consumer what the service does on an empty database, and in HSDD a producer's gate proves what its contract states. booking-api@v1 Validation already gives the properties no fixture can hold to the producer's own tests and the integration node together, never to the integration node alone; start-on-empty is such a property. The cost is a few lines in a phase not yet built (hsdd/verify/ holds no simple-login.backend.7 verification doc), so a rewrite in place keeps the phase id and changes no contract. hsdd-phase-plan's append mode is the owning skill's way to rewrite an unshipped phase when the invocation names it. Evidence that simple-login.backend.7 had shipped, or that `start` cannot be pointed at a test database without the schema, would have made the second option lead.

question: Q-079: from simple-login.backend.7 the service needs PostgreSQL, and until simple-login.integration.3 merges the shipped rig starts backend/src/server.ts with neither `db:up` nor DATABASE_URL. Does the backend's plan carry a landing note on simple-login.backend.7?

options.label: leave it with simple-login.integration.3
options.consequence: No backend change. simple-login.integration.3's Dependencies keep the landing note on the side that owns the root scripts. In the window the root `npm test` still passes, because it runs `npm --prefix backend run gate` before the browser suite and from simple-login.backend.4 that gate starts PostgreSQL itself; `npm run dev` or `npm run e2e` alone fail until `db:up` runs, and simple-login.backend.7's exit message names it.

options.label: carry a landing note to simple-login.backend.7's Dependencies
options.consequence: The inserted phase-plan-append also adds a line tying the merge of simple-login.backend.7 to simple-login.integration.3, which the hard edge schedules after the backend ships. It couples the backend developer's delivery to an integration phase, although PRD v2 Team and delivery has the two developers ship separately.

why: The window Q-079 names does not break the root gate: package.json's `test` runs the backend's gate before the e2e suite, and from simple-login.backend.4 that gate runs `db:up`, so PostgreSQL is up and `meeting_rooms` exists when the shipped rig starts the service on its default DATABASE_URL (e2e/fixtures.ts passes the environment through). What remains is running `dev` or `e2e` on their own, which simple-login.backend.7's exit message naming `npm --prefix backend run db:up` already covers. The fix is in the root scripts that simple-login.integration owns (simple-login.integration.3 (a)), whose Dependencies already say to land it with the backend's PostgreSQL work. A CI job or root script that ran the browser suite without the backend's gate first would have made a backend-side note worth its coupling.

question: S23 reports that the backend header's Isolation strategy says 'the service itself opens no port' while the shipped start test in backend/test/server.test.ts listens on 127.0.0.1 at an ephemeral port, and left the sentence unchanged. Rework, route, or leave?

options.label: Rework S23 with the finding
options.consequence: The step that owns the header corrects the sentence S09 wrote; the artifact commit is no longer empty.

options.label: Route a must-address to simple-login.backend
options.consequence: Another spec-touch on the same node later, for one sentence the current step can fix.

options.label: Leave it
options.consequence: A false sentence stays in the backend's live header and reaches every backend phase context.

why: The sentence is in S23's own target and write set, the step read it and knew it false, and the review rule sends such a sentence back to the step. The finding is narrow: restate the Isolation strategy's port clause so it matches the shipped start test, in the header and its embedded copy in hsdd/spec/simple-login.md. A sentence outside the step's write set would have been routed instead.

question: DEC-207: the Isolation strategy's closing clause 'no browser, and the service itself opens no port' is false against backend/test/server.test.ts, whose `start` test calls `start(0)` and listens on 127.0.0.1 at an ephemeral port. How is the clause restated, in the node's header and in the embedded summary in hsdd/spec/simple-login.md?

options.label: no fixed port; only the `start` test listens, at a port the system picks
options.consequence: True against the shipped tests: server.test.ts's `start(0)` is the only call that listens, every other test uses `app.inject()` or none, and nothing needs port 3000 free. It keeps the point the clause made, that the node's tests need no running service at a known address, and it stays true when simple-login.backend.7's `start` test runs on a test database (DEC-205).

options.label: drop the clause, keep 'no browser'
options.consequence: True, but it loses the statement that the tests need no fixed port, which tells a reader why the gate can run beside `npm run dev` or the browser suite holding port 3000.

options.label: restore the pre-S09 'no browser and no open port needed'
options.consequence: Still false: the shipped `start` test opens a port, and it has since simple-login.backend.2.

chosen: no fixed port; only the `start` test listens, at a port the system picks
why: The clause must be true against the shipped test (DEC-207). A grep of backend/test finds one listener, `start(0)` in server.test.ts, on 127.0.0.1; backend/src/server.ts listens only inside `start`. Port 0 lets the system pick the port, so no test depends on 3000 being free, which is the isolation property the clause was there to state. The PostgreSQL connections the booking tests open are client sockets, not listeners, so 'listens' is the precise verb. Had another test listened on a fixed port, the clause would have had to name it instead.

question: S23 routed Q-084, an insert-step for a phase-plan-append on simple-login.backend that rewrites the unshipped simple-login.backend.7 in place, so its start test proves on an empty database what booking-api@v1's Development address now promises (S21's request answer). Accept it, and does the intake record's insert rule also call for a reconcile on the node?

options.label: Accept Q-084 and add a reconcile on simple-login.backend after it
options.consequence: Two more steps; the backend's gate proves the promise the integration rig's global setup relies on, and any pending entry the rewrite emits is drained before the report.

options.label: Accept Q-084 only
options.consequence: One step; a pending entry the rewrite emitted would be left in the backend's section, which the done condition refuses.

options.label: Reject it
options.consequence: The promise is proved only by the integration suite, against a running Compose service, late in the build.

chosen: Accept Q-084 and add a reconcile on simple-login.backend after it
why: The intake record's insert rule names this case: a reconcile's request answer made after a node's append that alters what its unshipped phases implement or replay adds a phase-plan-append that rewrites those phases in place and a reconcile on that node, before the align. backend.7 has no verification doc, so it is unshipped and may be rewritten. A shipped backend.7 would have changed this to a new phase.
